about: Master copy of the dose-occupancy values shared by the Psychopharmacology Visualiser and HyperTaper. Edit this file only, then run `node scripts/sync-ed50-bank.mjs` to regenerate ed50-bank.js (and copy this file into HyperTaper if it sits next to this repo).
model: occupancy (%) = emax_pct x dose / (dose + ed50_mg). ed50_mg is the daily dose giving half of the maximum occupancy. When emax_pct is null the source did not report a maximum and 100% is assumed.

evidenceLevels.reported: ED50 stated in the cited source.
evidenceLevels.back-calculated: ED50 solved from dose-occupancy tables printed in the cited source, using the maximum occupancy that source reports.
evidenceLevels.fitted: ED50 fitted to dose-occupancy figures in the cited source.
evidenceLevels.derived: Not measured for this drug: worked out from another drug's value with a stated conversion. Treat as a rough estimate.
evidenceLevels.none: No usable human occupancy data found. Enter a value by hand if you have one.

sorensen2022.citation: Sørensen A, Ruhé HG, Munkholm K. The relationship between dose and serotonin transporter occupancy of antidepressants: a systematic review. Mol Psychiatry 2022;27:192–201.

lako2013.citation: Lako IM, van den Heuvel ER, Knegtering H, Bruggeman R, Taxis K. Estimating dopamine D2 receptor occupancy for doses of 8 antipsychotics: a meta-analysis. J Clin Psychopharmacol 2013;33:675–681.

horowitz2021.citation: Horowitz MA, Jauhar S, Natesan S, Murray RM, Taylor D. A method for tapering antipsychotic treatment that may minimize the risk of relapse. Schizophr Bull 2021;47:1116–1129.

volkow1998.citation: Volkow ND, Wang GJ, Fowler JS, et al. Dopamine transporter occupancies in the human brain induced by therapeutic doses of oral methylphenidate. Am J Psychiatry 1998;155:1325–1331.

maudsley2024.citation: Horowitz MA, Taylor D. The Maudsley Deprescribing Guidelines. Wiley-Blackwell, 2024 (diazepam tapering tables).

ashton2002.citation: Ashton CH. Benzodiazepines: How They Work and How to Withdraw (the Ashton Manual), 2002. Table of approximate equivalent doses to diazepam 10 mg.

citalopram.name: Citalopram
citalopram.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022 (from the individual PET studies it reviewed).

escitalopram.name: Escitalopram
escitalopram.method: Half the citalopram ED50 (3.4 mg), because escitalopram is the active half (S-enantiomer) of citalopram. Sørensen et al. 2022 did not report an escitalopram ED50.

sertraline.name: Sertraline
sertraline.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.

paroxetine.name: Paroxetine
paroxetine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.

fluoxetine.name: Fluoxetine
fluoxetine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.
fluoxetine.note: Its long-acting metabolite (norfluoxetine) slows the fall in occupancy after each dose change.

fluvoxamine.name: Fluvoxamine
fluvoxamine.method: Sørensen et al. 2022 found only one small fluvoxamine study and reported no ED50.

venlafaxine.name: Venlafaxine
venlafaxine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022 (extended-release venlafaxine).
venlafaxine.note: Modified-release capsules: do not split or crush.

desvenlafaxine.name: Desvenlafaxine
desvenlafaxine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.
desvenlafaxine.note: Modified-release tablets: do not split or crush.

duloxetine.name: Duloxetine
duloxetine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.

vortioxetine.name: Vortioxetine
vortioxetine.method: ED50 reported in Sørensen et al. 2022.

mirtazapine.name: Mirtazapine
mirtazapine.method: No verified human dose-occupancy curve found.

amitriptyline.name: Amitriptyline
amitriptyline.method: No verified human dose-occupancy curve found.

nortriptyline.name: Nortriptyline
nortriptyline.method: No verified human dose-occupancy curve found.

haloperidol.name: Haloperidol
haloperidol.method: Solved from Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 3 (e.g. 1 mg = 55.7%, 4 mg = 79.0%, 10 mg = 86.3%), which uses the Lako et al. 2013 curve; maximum occupancy 91.9% from Lako et al. 2013.

risperidone.name: Risperidone
risperidone.method: Solved from the risperidone column of Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 4 (reproduces every step to 2 significant figures); maximum occupancy 92.4% from Lako et al. 2013.

olanzapine.name: Olanzapine
olanzapine.method: Solved from the olanzapine column of Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 4; maximum occupancy 96.5% from Lako et al. 2013.

quetiapine.name: Quetiapine
quetiapine.method: Solved from the quetiapine column of Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 4; maximum D2 occupancy 49.1% from Lako et al. 2013 (wide confidence interval, 18.7–79.6%).
quetiapine.note: Low and short-lived D2 occupancy: withdrawal effects at low doses are probably driven more by H1 and other receptors than by D2.

clozapine.name: Clozapine
clozapine.method: Solved from the clozapine column of Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 4; maximum D2 occupancy 61.7% from Lako et al. 2013.
clozapine.note: Cholinergic rebound is common when clozapine is reduced quickly.

amisulpride.name: Amisulpride
amisulpride.method: Solved from the amisulpride column of Horowitz et al. 2021 Table 4; maximum occupancy 85.0% from Lako et al. 2013.

aripiprazole.name: Aripiprazole
aripiprazole.method: Horowitz et al. 2021 left aripiprazole out because the Lako et al. 2013 curve fitted the data poorly.

paliperidone.name: Paliperidone
paliperidone.method: No verified human dose-occupancy curve found.
paliperidone.note: Modified-release tablets: do not split or crush.

methylphenidate.name: Methylphenidate
methylphenidate.method: Fitted to the mean DAT occupancies in Volkow et al. 1998 (5 mg 12%, 10 mg 40%, 20 mg 54%, 40 mg 72%, 60 mg 74%; single immediate-release doses, 2 h after the dose). The paper itself gives 0.25 mg/kg.
methylphenidate.note: Measured after single doses at peak level; occupancy later in the day will be lower.

diazepam.name: Diazepam
diazepam.method: 24.7 mg/day reproduces every occupancy figure in the Maudsley diazepam tapering tables.

alprazolam.name: Alprazolam
alprazolam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (alprazolam 0.5 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

clonazepam.name: Clonazepam
clonazepam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (clonazepam 0.5 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

lorazepam.name: Lorazepam
lorazepam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (lorazepam 1 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

nitrazepam.name: Nitrazepam
nitrazepam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (nitrazepam 10 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

oxazepam.name: Oxazepam
oxazepam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (oxazepam 20 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

temazepam.name: Temazepam
temazepam.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (temazepam 20 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

zolpidem.name: Zolpidem
zolpidem.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (zolpidem 20 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

zopiclone.name: Zopiclone
zopiclone.method: Diazepam value scaled by the Ashton Manual equivalence (zopiclone 15 mg ≈ diazepam 10 mg). Equivalence tables vary between sources.

gabapentin.name: Gabapentin
gabapentin.method: No human receptor-occupancy data. Absorption is saturable, so occupancy would not rise in proportion to dose anyway.
